metadata.title: OSS Map v3 — flagship three-axis scores
metadata.method: web-verified scoring per docs/specs/oss-map-v3/scoring-rubric-v3.md; adversarial version+openness verification pass
metadata.scope: flagship pilot set (~24 intended; 32 scored incl. variants)
metadata.note: Directional v3 scores for the flagship set. Long tail not yet scored. Every non-null value carries sources in the product record.

products.version_note: OLMo 2 family (1B/7B/13B/32B), base + Instruct. Latest 32B-Instruct (0325) and 1B (0425, updated May 2025). Verified existing June 2026; succeeded by OLMo 3 announced late 2025/2026.

openness.components: weights:open(Apache-2.0);data:open(Dolma/Tulu, all stages incl pre/mid/post-training);code:open(training code+recipes+logs);checkpoints:open(thousands of intermediate);license:Apache-2.0(OSI)

adoption.note: ATOM Report (Apr 2026) measures ~14.8M cumulative downloads for the OLMo family on Hugging Face; OLMo 2 1B alone ~323k downloads. Falls in 1-10M cumulative downloads band. Strong in research/interpretability circles but small vs Qwen/Llama scale.

capability.note: OLMo 2 32B is the most capable; reported competitive with GPT-3.5-Turbo / GPT-4o-mini class and Qwen 2.5 on academic benchmarks but below current frontier open models (DeepSeek-V4, Qwen 3.6). Mid-tier capability — the value proposition is full openness, not raw SOTA.

products.version_note: Pythia suite: 16 models, 70M-12B params (8 sizes x Pile/deduped-Pile), 154 intermediate checkpoints each. Released 2023 (arXiv 2304.01373); remains the standard interpretability/training-dynamics suite as of June 2026.

openness.components: weights:open(Apache-2.0);data:open(the Pile, with dataloader reconstruction tools);code:open(training+analysis code, GitHub);checkpoints:open(154 per model);license:Apache-2.0(OSI)

adoption.note: Heavily used as a research/interpretability benchmark suite (de facto standard for training-dynamics studies); cited extensively. Hugging Face download volume across the 16 models is in the 100k-1M aggregate range — meaningful for research but not production deployment. Honest signal: research adoption, not end-user scale.

capability.note: Not built for capability. Pythia models (max 12B, 2023-era Pile training) are intentionally research instruments for studying scaling/learning dynamics, not competitive on modern capability benchmarks. Scored 1 on a capability axis where the comparison set is 2026 frontier models.

products.version_note: Llama 4 herd, released April 2025: Scout (17B active / 109B total MoE, 10M-token context) and Maverick (17B active / 400B total MoE, 1M-token context), natively multimodal. Behemoth still unreleased/preview as of June 2026. Both Scout/Maverick verified live on HF June 2026.

openness.components: weights:open(downloadable on HF);data:closed;code:partial(inference/utils via llama-models, no training code);license:Llama-4-Community(non-OSI: 700M MAU commercial cap as of Apr 2025 + no-compete/no-train-competing-LLM clause)

adoption.note: ATOM Report (Apr 2026): Llama family ~476.0M cumulative HF downloads (second to Qwen). Llama 4 specifically is a fraction of that and lost derivative-base share (Meta's new-fine-tune share fell to ~11% by Feb 2026 from a 44% peak). Family-level 1-10M+ easily; Llama 4 alone solidly in the 1-10M band.

capability.note: Maverick (instruct) reports MMLU-Pro 80.5, GPQA Diamond 69.8; positioned at/above GPT-4o and Gemini 2.0 Flash at launch (Apr 2025). By June 2026 this is mid-tier vs DeepSeek-V4 / Qwen 3.6 frontier open models. Scout's long-context retrieval reported weak (Fiction.LiveBench 15.6% at 128K).

products.version_note: DeepSeek-V3.2, 671B total / 37B active MoE, introduces DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA). Open V3.2 + V3.2-Speciale (gold-medal IMO/IOI reasoning) released; Speciale dated Dec 1 2025; tech report arXiv 2512.02556. Verified live June 2026.

openness.components: weights:open(MIT, on HF);data:closed(training-data synthesis described in report but corpus not released);code:partial(inference code in HF repo; no full training pipeline);license:MIT(OSI-style permissive, no use restrictions)

adoption.note: ATOM Report (Apr 2026): China open models reached ~1.15B cumulative HF downloads with DeepSeek a primary driver; DeepSeek-V3.2 widely served (OpenRouter, multiple inference providers) with sustained post-launch production usage and frontier-at-10x-lower-cost positioning. Real usage well into the >10M-equivalent band across web app + API + derivatives.

capability.note: Tech report (arXiv 2512.02556): MMLU-Pro 85.0, GPQA Diamond 82.4, SWE-bench Verified 77.2; Speciale variant earns gold-medal IMO/IOI reasoning and AIME 2025 96.0. Near-frontier open model; sits just below DeepSeek-V4-Pro on the same family's curve.

products.version_note: DeepSeek-V4-Pro, 1.6T total / 49B active MoE, 1M-token context, hybrid CSA+HCA attention. Released April 24 2026 under MIT, alongside V4-Flash (284B). V4-Pro-Max = max-reasoning mode. Verified live June 2026.

openness.components: weights:open(MIT, on HF, both Pro and Flash);data:closed;code:partial(inference/serving; no training pipeline or data);license:MIT(permissive, no use restrictions)

adoption.note: Released Apr 24 2026 — ~6 weeks of production at scoring time. Available open-weights + API (permanent pricing set May 22 2026) and served across providers (OpenRouter, DeepInfra). Strong early traction consistent with DeepSeek family scale, but too recent to confirm >10M-equivalent reach independently; placed at 4 pending sustained data.

capability.note: SWE-bench Verified 80.6% (trails Claude Opus 4.6 by ~0.2), MMLU-Pro 87.5, GPQA Diamond 90.1, LiveCodeBench Pass@1 93.5 (reported best of any model). V4-Pro-Max described as the strongest open-source model available — at/near closed frontier on coding and reasoning.

products.version_note: Qwen3.6 series, released early-mid 2026: open-weight variants incl Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (MoE, Apr 16 2026) and dense Qwen3.6-27B (Apr 22 2026), plus hosted flagship tiers Qwen3.6-Plus and Qwen3.6-Max (Preview) that are proprietary/API-only. GitHub QwenLM/Qwen3.6 verified live June 2026.

openness.components: weights:open(Apache-2.0 for open variants e.g. 27B/35B-A3B);data:closed;code:partial(inference/usage code on GitHub; no training pipeline/data);license:mixed(open variants Apache-2.0; Plus/Max flagship tiers proprietary, commercial-restricted/API-only)

adoption.note: ATOM Report (Apr 2026): Qwen family ~942.1M cumulative HF downloads (>50% of all global open-source downloads), overtook Llama in Sept 2025; >113,000 derivative models (>200,000 incl tagged); 69% of new fine-tunes by Feb 2026 build on Qwen. Qwen 3.6 is the current flagship generation of that dominant family — unambiguously >10M reach.

capability.note: Dense Qwen3.6-27B: SWE-bench Verified 77.2, Terminal-Bench 2.0 59.3 (reported matching Claude 4.5 Opus class), outperforming a 397B MoE on agentic coding. Flagship Qwen3.6-Plus reported matching Claude Opus 4.5 on SWE-bench/Terminal-Bench. Frontier-tier open family.

products.version_note: Kimi K2.6, 1T total / 32B active MoE (384 experts, MLA), 256K context, 400M-param MoonViT vision encoder. Released April 20 2026 (rolled to all subscribers Apr 13). Verified live on HF June 2026.

openness.components: weights:open(downloadable on HF);data:closed;code:partial(inference/deploy; no training data or full pipeline);license:Modified-MIT(standard MIT below 100M MAU / $20M monthly rev; above thresholds requires 'Kimi K2' UI attribution — attribution-only, not a use cap)

adoption.note: Free on kimi.com + Kimi app + API + Kimi Code; partners Vercel, Baseten, Ollama, Factory.ai validated K2.6 in production (Vercel reports >50% improvement on Next.js benchmark). OpenRouter shows sustained post-launch usage spikes indicating genuine production adoption. No exact download/user count published; placed at 4 (1-10M-equivalent) on production-traction signal.

capability.note: SWE-bench Verified 80.2%, SWE-bench Pro 58.6% (up from 50.7% in K2.5), Terminal-Bench 2.0 66.7% (up from 50.8%). Reported tying GPT-5.5 on coding and beating some top US models; specialized for long-horizon agentic coding (300-agent swarms, 4,000 coordinated steps). Frontier-tier for agentic/coding work.

products.version_note: Mistral Large 3 (mistral-large-3-25-12), announced 2 Dec 2025. Sparse MoE, 41B active / 675B total params. Base + instruct released; reasoning variant announced but not shipped as of mid-2026.

adoption.note: Distributed via Hugging Face (NVFP4 checkpoint, vLLM-ready) and Microsoft Foundry as a production model. No published hard download/user counts found; level 3 reflects multi-platform enterprise distribution rather than a verified usage_volume number.

capability.note: Debuts #2 in LMArena OSS non-reasoning category (#6 among all OSS models). Per-benchmark MMLU-Pro/GPQA/SWE-bench not given in the launch post.

products.version_note: Gemma 3 family (1B, 4B, 12B, 27B), released 12 Mar 2025. 4B/12B/27B are vision-language; 1B is text-only. Both pretrained and instruction-tuned weights released. (Successor Gemma 4 has since appeared but Gemma 3 is the scored product.)

adoption.note: Gemma family is among the most-downloaded open model families on Hugging Face; Gemma 3 variants run on consumer hardware and are widely deployed via HF, Ollama, and Google AI tooling. Family-level downloads are in the tens-of-millions+ range.

capability.note: Gemma 3 27B-IT: MMLU-Pro 67.5, GPQA Diamond 42.4 (0-shot), LMArena/Chatbot Arena Elo ~1338 (top-10, above much larger non-thinking OSS models). Strong for size but a non-reasoning, mid-2025 model.

products.version_note: GLM-5.1 released 7 Apr 2026 by Z.ai (formerly Zhipu AI). Post-training upgrade on GLM-5 base; 744B-param MoE. Weights on Hugging Face under MIT.

adoption.note: Widely covered as a top open coding model and available via Z.ai API, OpenRouter, and HF; strong reported uptake but only ~2 months old at scoring time, no verified hard user/download count. Level 3 reflects reported traction, not a measured usage_volume figure.

capability.note: SWE-Bench Pro 58.4 (reported #1 at release, edging GPT-5.4 57.7 and Claude Opus 4.6 57.3); Terminal-Bench 2.0 63.5. Frontier-tier agentic coding for an open-weights model.

products.version_note: Phi-4, 14B dense model, weights released on Hugging Face under MIT (full release Jan 2025 following Dec 2024 announcement). Reasoning variants (Phi-4-reasoning / -reasoning-plus) released later under open weights but are separate SKUs; this record scores base Phi-4 14B.

adoption.note: Phi-4 is a widely downloaded small model on Hugging Face, distributed via Azure AI Foundry, Ollama, and many local-inference stacks; download volume for the Phi-4 line is in the millions range. Level 4 reflects broad small-model adoption.

capability.note: 14B model with outsized math/reasoning: ~56.1% on graduate-level (GPQA-style) science questions, 80.4% on competition math, strong AMC results; reportedly beats GPT-4 (its teacher) on some STEM. Strong-for-size but a small/older model vs 2026 frontier.

products.version_note: Falcon 3 family (1B, 3B, 7B, 10B), released 17 Dec 2024 by TII. Trained on 14T tokens. Sub-13B SLMs; now a dated generation relative to 2026 frontier.

adoption.note: Available on Hugging Face with moderate uptake at launch as a sub-13B SLM; no large verified usage figures and relevance has faded against newer SLMs. Level 2 reflects modest reported traction.

capability.note: Falcon3-10B-Base: MMLU 73.1, MMLU-Pro 42.5, GSM8K 83.0; Falcon3-7B-Base: MMLU 67.4, MMLU-Pro 39.2. Competitive among sub-13B in 2024 but low vs 2026 frontier.

Company committed to releasing technical report + open weights within ~10 days, but as of scoring the weights are NOT on Hugging Face and the license is unconfirmed (predecessor M2.7 used a non-commercial-restricted license).

capability.note: Vendor reports SWE-Bench Pro scores edging out GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro, but benchmarks are vendor-run and not independently verified at scoring time; declining to assign a score to avoid relying on unverified claims.

products.version_note: Scored on Nemotron 3 Super (120B hybrid MoE, 12B active, 1M context), released 11 Mar 2026 at GTC. Family also includes Nemotron 3 Nano (Dec 2025) and Nemotron 3 Nano Omni (Apr 2026, 30B multimodal). products.version_note: OpenAI GPT-5, released Aug 7, 2025; default ChatGPT model. Successor versions (5.2/5.4/5.5) shipped through April 2026, but the scored entity is GPT-5 itself, which remains in service via API/ChatGPT.

adoption.note: GPT-5 was rolled out as the default model for logged-in ChatGPT users (Aug 2025). ChatGPT reached ~900M weekly active users (Feb 2026) and ~1B by May 2026, far exceeding the >10M threshold. Adoption attributed to the surface GPT-5 powers, not a standalone GPT-5 download count.

verdicts.issue: The license sub-component is partly inaccurate. The claim includes a "no-compete/no-train-competing-LLM clause" in the Llama 4 Community License. Verified directly against the license text (llama.com/llama4/license): Section 2 contains the 700M MAU commercial cap (confirmed), and Section 1.b.i requires derivative models to include "Llama" in their name plus "Built with Llama" attribution — but there is NO clause prohibiting use of outputs to train a competing/other LLM. That no-train-competitor restriction existed in the Llama 2 license and was dropped/relaxed in Llama 3.x and Llama 4; the claim appears to conflate Llama 2 terms. Everything else verifies: model released Apr 5, 2025 (not forward-dated); HF page meta-llama/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E exists with downloadable BF16 safetensors weights (~16K downloads/month, plus int4/fp8 quants); data is closed (only high-level ~40T-token description, no dataset); code is partial (inference/utils via llama-models/llama-cookbook, no training code); license is non-OSI. The overall "restricted" class is defensible regardless of the clause error, since the non-OSI MAU cap plus naming/attribution requirements alone justify it.
verdicts.suggested_fix: In the license component, replace "no-compete/no-train-competing-LLM clause" with the accurate Llama 4 restrictions: "700M MAU commercial cap (Section 2) + mandatory 'Llama' naming for derivatives and 'Built with Llama' attribution (Section 1.b.i)". Do not attribute a no-train-competitor clause to Llama 4 (that was Llama 2). Keep the "restricted" class. Sources are largely good; the royfactory.net link is a third-party blog — recommend anchoring the license claim on the primary source https://www.llama.com/llama4/license/ or https://github.com/meta-llama/llama-models/blob/main/models/llama4/LICENSE.

verdicts.issue: No blocking issue. Entry verified against the authoritative Hugging Face model card (zai-org/GLM-5.1), which confirms MIT license and downloadable open Safetensors weights, with no public training data or training code released (only weights plus a technical report and inference repo) — consistent with the claimed open_weights class (weights:open(MIT); data:closed; code:closed). Released April 7, 2026 by Z.ai (formerly Zhipu AI); not forward-dated/hallucinated. Two caveats worth noting: (1) the three claimed sources are SEO/aggregator blogs (buildfastwithai, mlhive, llm-stats) rather than primary sources, and one (mlhive) could not be independently confirmed; (2) a minor parameter-count inconsistency appears across sources (744B vs 754B), with HF/llm-stats reporting 754B MoE / 40B active — this does not affect the openness classification.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Add primary sources to strengthen citations: the Hugging Face model card (https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.1) and the official Z.ai blog (https://z.ai/blog/glm-5.1). Optionally drop or downgrade the mlhive source, which could not be verified, and standardize the parameter count to 754B (40B active) per the model card.

verdicts.issue: Minor: the claimed license string is written as "TII-Falcon-License-2.0" but the official/exact name is "TII Falcon-LLM License 2.0" (the "LLM" token is missing). This is cosmetic and does not affect the classification.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Normalize the license label to the exact official name "TII Falcon-LLM License 2.0" (Apache 2.0-based + Acceptable Use Policy, non-OSI). All else confirmed: Falcon3 family (1B/3B/7B/10B Base+Instruct) released Dec 2024 by Technology Innovation Institute; weights open on Hugging Face (safetensors), training data and training code not released — consistent with "restricted" / weights:open;data:closed;code:closed.

verdicts.issue: Minor (non-blocking): the "data:open" claim slightly overstates completeness. NVIDIA explicitly states it releases only "all the data for which we hold redistribution rights," so the pretraining/post-training corpora are substantially but not fully released. Everything else (weights open on HF in BF16/FP8/NVFP4, code/recipes + 21 RL env configs on the Nemotron Developer GitHub repo, NVIDIA Nemotron Open Model License = permissive, commercial, non-OSI) is fully corroborated by NVIDIA's own newsroom/blog/research-labs/technical-report and independent coverage (VentureBeat, Artificial Analysis, OpenRouter, Decrypt). Model is real and released (Nemotron 3 Super launched March 11, 2026 at GTC; Nano available; Ultra unveiled June 1, 2026 at Computex) — not a hallucinated or forward-dated version.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Soften the data component from "data:open" to "data:mostly-open (subject to NVIDIA redistribution rights)" to precisely reflect that not 100% of the training corpus is released. No change to the "open_weights" class, which is correct given the non-OSI permissive license.

verdicts.issue: The bare "Gemini 3.5" is not a released model SKU. The cited Google blog post and Gemini API docs describe Gemini 3.5 as a model *family*; the only generally-available released model is "Gemini 3.5 Flash" (GA May 19, 2026, API ID gemini-3.5-flash). "Gemini 3.5 Pro" was announced as internal-only with a planned rollout the following month and is not confirmed GA as of early June 2026. The entry conflates the family name with a shippable version. The openness class itself is correct: all Gemini 3.5 models are API-only/proprietary with weights, data, and code closed (in contrast to Google's open-weights Gemma line), so closed;weights:closed;data:closed;code:closed;Proprietary(API-only) is accurate.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Rename the entry to "Gemini 3.5 Flash" (the GA SKU, API ID gemini-3.5-flash, released 2026-05-19) and keep the closed/proprietary classification. Optionally add a separate "Gemini 3.5 Pro" row only once it is confirmed publicly released. Update the primary source link to the model-specific docs page (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models/gemini-3.5-flash) alongside the blog announcement.
